markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize **a controlled moderate-negative sampling ablation within the existing BERT4Rec**. The historical 0.5900 score is context, not a reproduced improvement or evidence for harder negatives.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) K=16 cross-entropy provides a candidate-count control, but auditing the actual baseline remains necessary. Otherwise, loss and sampling changes become confounded. (2) Fixing terminal allocation and reconstruction isolates candidate construction more closely. Extra mining still changes compute and candidate exposure. (3) Every category has zero inspected margin batches. This establishes missing measurement, not failed masking or poor separation.

**Insights from related work.** (1) AHNS [2] uses positive-dependent hardness and reports harder negatives earlier and easier ones later. It does not validate the proposed epoch-based curriculum. (2) Sampling theory [5–7] shows that model-selected, uncorrected candidates define a sampler-dependent surrogate. Neither BPR theory nor logQ correction transfers automatically to this loss. (3) Temporal and content studies [3–4] motivate alternatives, but establish neither stronger recency nor scratch-trained text gains here. (4) Sampled-metric and selection-bias research [8–10] limits claims from repeated validation comparisons. Fixed candidates support controlled benchmark comparisons without establishing full-catalog superiority.

The framework separates **candidate discrimination**, **historical context**, and **item identification**. Pipeline observability supports each direction but is distinct from recommendation quality.

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension has a positive and negative assessment.

| Idea | Scores | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed moderate-negative curriculum | 2/6/5/5/5 | O: precise adaptation / established sampling; P: interpretable ablation / arbitrary schedule; U: challenges broad alternatives / indirect identification; M: restores coverage / separation unknown; D: localized scoring / integration and compute controls |
| Positive-conditioned hardness | 3/7/5/4/6 | O: sequential adaptation / AHNS precedent; P: adaptive difficulty / transfer uncertain; U: contextual competition / uncertain negatives; M: measurable selection / margins unavailable; D: compact rule / calibration and loss mismatch |
| Learned signed time-gap bias | 4/7/7/3/6 | O: flexible adaptation / existing biases; P: context modeling / sparse timing; U: targets stale interests / direction unproven; M: measurable sensitivity / outcomes omitted; D: few parameters / writer changes |
| Joint scratch-trained title residual | 4/7/8/3/7 | O: constrained integration / established fusion; P: finer identification / sparse text; U: specific connections / similarity can mislead; M: testable features / alignment is inconclusive; D: simple pooling / vocabulary and masking work |

Retain the first idea for feasibility: epochs 1–20 use uniform K=16; later updates use twelve uniform negatives and four moderate-ranked candidates from 32 uniform draws. This is an exploratory fixed policy, not AHNS. It targets broad alternatives displacing specific matches and weak identifiable relevance, both indirectly. Repair diagnostic coverage separately; do not claim it demonstrates algorithmic benefit. Preserve corruption and compare against uniform K=16 with declared compute accounting. Track duplicate pressure, repeated-item exposure, and false-negative risk. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10 against 99 unique negatives; reserve confirmatory claims for the untouched final evaluation.

idea.description: Test a predeclared fixed moderate-negative curriculum against uniform K=16 candidate cross-entropy in the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Each configuration independently trains exactly one model per category, and comparison configurations are never combined at inference. Candidate selection uses detached scores from the same current network. Pair the experiment with bounded production-record capture and a functioning diagnostic loader to address missing measurement. This is an exploratory sampling policy rather than a reproduction of AHNS or a full-catalog likelihood estimator.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broadly related alternatives displacing specifically supported choices and recommendations lacking identifiable connections to history. Moderately competitive negatives may encourage finer contextual distinctions, but this connection is indirect: interaction supervision alone cannot establish compatibility, ownership, redundancy, current intent, or an identifiable semantic explanation. These two user-facing failures motivate the experiment without establishing that it remedies them. The current quantitative diagnosis establishes a model-facing observability failure: zero inspected margin batches, missing consumed-pipeline provenance, and unavailable deployed predictor parity. It does not establish inadequate positive-negative separation, failed production masking, harmful embedding collapse, or a need for harder negatives. Restoring measured diagnostic coverage addresses that failure independently of any recommendation gain. At 20% progress, a localized sampling ablation is preferable to adding temporal or text architecture changes simultaneously. A positive-conditioned AHNS-style adaptation remains a follow-up because its original BPR/MF formulation does not directly specify an appropriate K=16 masked-target cross-entropy rule.
idea.implementation_notes:
This remains an integration specification with executable core loss logic, not a replacement train.py: the supplied baseline source, checkpoint-selection implementation and predictor-writer interfaces are absent from this writing input. No training or new measurements have been performed. Do not reconstruct unspecified host behavior or claim that the helper alone reproduces an experiment.

Baseline and comparisons: audit the actual supplied objective, negative count, proposal, eligibility rules, replacement policy, loss reductions, terminal allocation, optimizer, schedule, clipping, stopping, checkpoint-selection and tie rules before editing. Preserve the unchanged supplied baseline as the practical anchor without reading other trials or reusing checkpoints. The primary sampling comparison is uniform K=16 CE versus curriculum K=16 CE, initialized independently from the same cold start with seed 42. If the host baseline differs from uniform K=16 CE, distinguish the baseline-to-treatment combined intervention from this matched sampling ablation. Do not silently infer a BCE/K=1 baseline. The earlier count-matched baseline-objective control remains a separate optional comparison when needed to distinguish loss from negative-count effects; it must not be bundled into the sampling claim. Avoid duplicate training when configurations are actually equivalent. Complete all four categories for each inspected configuration; do not select different configurations category by category from this comparison.

Predeclared policy: use one-based epochs. Epochs 1–20 use sixteen uniform eligible negative draws per supervised target. From epoch 21 onward, retain the first twelve of those sixteen draws and add four candidates selected from a separate pool of 32 uniform eligible draws. Score the pool with the same current network and the same stochastic features used by the loss, detach the selection computation, sort descending with stable ties, and select one-based ranks 9, 13, 17 and 21. This avoids selecting the eight highest-ranked pool entries but does not guarantee easy negatives or exclude a selected item that also appears in the retained uniform draws. The epoch schedule, pool size and ranks are fixed hypotheses, not AHNS-derived or optimal settings; do not tune them after inspecting treatment results. AHNS instead uses positive-specific adjustable target scores and reports hardness decreasing as positive confidence increases. Its evidence does not establish this curriculum or transfer from BPR/MF to masked BERT4Rec CE.

Negative eligibility and multiplicity: exclude the positive target, PAD and MASK, and preserve the baseline's existing training-history exclusions. Do not add broader history exclusions silently, consult validation/test interactions, or treat unobserved items as verified dislikes. Preserve the audited baseline replacement policy for each draw set. With replacement, retain repeated entries and record multiplicity. Without replacement, draw each set under the declared baseline policy; independent sets can still overlap, and concatenating them does not guarantee sixteen unique negatives. Explicitly document this cross-set behavior in both configurations. When the pool cannot be constructed under that policy, use the predeclared uniform K=16 fallback if it is feasible; otherwise apply the baseline's documented small-catalog or empty-eligible-set handling. Count all fallback and skipped cases, and guard against empty reductions. Do not invent a fallback after seeing results.

Objective: for positive score p and sixteen negative scores n_j, use L=logsumexp([p,n_1,...,n_16])-p, with numerically stable cross-entropy. Preserve the baseline's across-target/example weighting; returning unreduced losses does not establish that simple averaging matches it. Use no logQ adjustment and describe the result as a sampler-dependent candidate-ranking surrogate. The moderate-rank selector has a model- and pool-dependent distribution; uniform proposal probabilities are not its selection probabilities. Applying a uniform logQ correction would therefore be unjustified, and treating the always-included positive like a sampled negative would add another error. BPR partial-AUC results do not establish an equivalent theorem for this CE objective. If item j occurs m times, its denominator contribution is m*exp(s_j), equivalent to one entry at s_j+log(m); its aggregate gradient is not simply m times the single-entry gradient because normalization also changes. Deduplication would define another intervention and must not be introduced in only one arm.

Randomness and selection determinism: initialize Python, NumPy, PyTorch and any loader workers reproducibly from training seed 42. Use fixed category ordering and explicit purpose-separated generators for user/window selection, masking, standard negatives, mining pools and diagnostics. Do not use Python's randomized hash. Keep the extra pool generator isolated so mining does not change windows or corruption. Use the same stream scheme in both matched configurations; distinguish it from the unchanged host anchor if the anchor used a shared stream. Compare recorded user/window/target/mask hashes across matched arms before claiming example matching. Run the pool scoring in the existing training mode with detached same-forward features; do not silently switch to eval mode for mining. If scoring itself introduces stochastic operations, declare and isolate their RNG behavior. Dropout makes selection stochastic even with detached features; fixed seeds do not imply identical optimization trajectories or cross-platform bitwise reproducibility.

Compute accounting: identical optimizer steps and final candidate count do not imply matched compute. After warm-up, the treatment scores 32 pool entries in addition to the final sixteen candidates and exposes more items during selection. Keep the primary comparison at matched epochs, batches and checkpoint rules, and explicitly report its additional GPU-seconds. If budget permits, add an exposure control that constructs and scores the same pool but selects four pool entries by a predeclared score-independent rule; this distinguishes score-based selection from merely sourcing candidates from an extra pool. Such a control may have different sampling dependence or unique-item coverage unless those details are matched and reported. It is not perfectly compute-identical without measuring runtime. A separately budgeted larger-uniform-candidate control can investigate candidate-count effects but changes the loss denominator. Do not describe any of these controls as simultaneously matching compute, exposure, and objective geometry without evidence. A runtime-limited comparison is a separate estimand and must have its stopping rule declared before results.

Protocol and budget: preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes—Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl—the supplied splits, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Honor the host SASREC_EPOCHS=200 default and do not raise the cap. Preserve the host validation schedule, stopping, checkpoint and tie rules. Every training run, diagnostic, debug attempt, failed comparison and optional control consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; concurrent slots do not reduce summed cost. Prioritize complete primary comparisons, record actual GPU time, and do not launch optional controls without enough remaining budget. Each configuration retains one selected checkpoint per category, with no checkpoint averaging or independent-model score fusion.

Production-linked diagnostics: capture at most four actually consumed production records per category, including stable training source-window/event identifiers, corruption and negative RNG information or replay state, candidate IDs, labels, same-forward detached logits, selected pool ranks and the reduction metadata needed for replay. Sample provenance must describe the actual model-selected candidates, not label them uniform. A seed alone cannot reconstruct model-ranked selection without corresponding scores/model state; retain the pool IDs and detached pool scores for these bounded records. Do not advance a live training iterator to obtain captures. Compare detached logits with the declared loss reduction without another forward, recording numerical tolerances. These bounded records do not establish fault prevalence, gradient correctness, exact restart, or checkpoint provenance unless those properties are separately checked. Keep detached captures bounded rather than storing autograd graphs.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), constructing its prompt from those measured values and definitions. Preserve view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Supply a disposable, independently seeded family-specific diagnostic loader yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L, with genuine reserved-mask targets and the fixed one-negative diagnostic protocol. Internal K-dimensional training negatives and bounded provenance remain outside this tuple. Actually inspect batches before reporting margins; record inspected batches, valid-target counts, invalid positions and reasons for missingness. In the supplied results zero inspected batches means zero coverage, not evidence of a production masking failure. Report baseline and treatment margins under the same diagnostic candidate draws, and retain logit-scale caveats. Negative-beats-positive frequency is invariant to a common positive score rescaling; raw margins and the margin<0.5 rate are not. Neither diagnostic is a held-out selection metric. Keep unavailable checks unavailable rather than treating them as passes.

Architecture and inference: preserve the supplied corrected BERT4Rec architecture, reserved tokens, mask corruption and terminal allocation. Hide supervised targets at their input positions and never expose shifted prediction labels through bidirectional inputs. Legitimate earlier occurrences of an item remain valid context. At inference retain the final L-1 observed history items, append MASK, left-pad to L, and read the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Require the baseline-supported capacity for appended-mask inference. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendations. Keep checkpoint configuration, item mappings, category routing and embedded predictor writer consistent even though only training changes. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Verify emitted-predictor versus checkpoint scores in a fresh process when a runner is available; live identity checks are insufficient. Until actually measured, deployed parity remains unavailable.

Validation and uncertainty: select solely by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10: 200 users per category, one positive and 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42. Do not alter the host evaluator, users, candidates, splits or selection metric. Report category hits/200, category HR@10 and equally weighted macro differences only from host measurements. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. The existing historical 0.5900 score is not a reproduced comparison or a treatment result. Fixed sampled candidates permit controlled comparisons but do not eliminate the possibility of model-order reversals relative to full-catalog evaluation.

If paired host per-user hit indicators are supplied, retain baseline and treatment indicators for the same users and run 10,000 bootstrap resamples with analysis seed 42, resampling 200 paired users within each category and recomputing the equally weighted four-category difference. Report the observed difference and percentile 95% interval; if paired records are unavailable, mark the interval unavailable. This describes exploratory user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted models and fixed candidates. It excludes training-seed variation, negative-candidate variation and adaptive selection bias; for the fixed finite benchmark the observed difference itself is deterministic. Record all inspected configurations, checkpoint evaluations, failures and selection rules. Ordinary post-search intervals do not correct validation overfitting. Freeze selection before the host's untouched final evaluation. Twenty training users' full-catalog simulator recommendations are a separate, limited qualitative setting, not evidence that sampled HR gains improve full-catalog usefulness.

Risks and alternatives: repeated targets and model-selected negatives can reinforce popularity shortcuts, over-penalize frequently selected items, and suppress genuine future positives. Keeping twelve uniform entries and avoiding the pool's top quartile limits the intervention but does not prove false-negative mitigation. Record unique negative counts, pool/final-set duplicates, fallback counts, selected-item exposure concentration and training-popularity strata using public training counts. These descriptive measurements do not identify true negatives or prove user benefit. Do not infer harmful collapse from angular alignment statistics alone. If the treatment fails, retain that outcome rather than tuning ranks repeatedly on the same validation set; consider the separately specified positive-conditioned hardness idea only as a new budgeted hypothesis. Temporal bias and jointly trained scratch text remain alternative directions, with matched architecture/writer changes and complete target-content masking required for text. Available information comprises public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. No unavailable ratings, reviews, item categories/prices/stores, simulator traits, target timestamps, extra datasets, pretrained weights or hidden test files may enter training, diagnostics or explanations.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def masked_candidate_ce(view, sequence, positive, uniform16,
                        mask_id, score_pairs, pool32=None, epoch=1):
    """Core loss, not a standalone train.py.

    sequence, positive: [B, L]
    uniform16: [B, L, 16], generated with audited eligibility semantics
    pool32: [B, L, 32], required after warm-up unless caller falls back
    epoch: one-based

    score_pairs(features, items) -> [T, C] must use the actual model's
    scoring head and preserve gradients. It is a host-specific adapter
    around view.predict_score, not an assumed broadcasting convention.
    Return per-target losses; caller applies the audited baseline reduction.
    """
    if epoch < 1:
        raise ValueError('epoch must be one-based')
    if sequence.shape != positive.shape:
        raise ValueError('sequence and positive shapes must match')
    if uniform16.shape != (*sequence.shape, 16):
        raise ValueError('uniform16 must have shape [B, L, 16]')

    valid = positive.gt(0)
    if not bool(valid.any()):
        raise ValueError('Caller must apply documented empty-target handling')
    if not bool(sequence[valid].eq(mask_id).all()):
        raise ValueError('Supervised positions must contain reserved MASK')

    features = view.log2feats(sequence)[valid]
    targets = positive[valid]
    uniform = uniform16[valid]
    negatives = uniform
    selection_record = None

    # Eligibility, catalog bounds, history exclusions and replacement
    # semantics are checked by the audited host sampler, not inferred here.
    if epoch > 20:
        if pool32 is None or pool32.shape != (*sequence.shape, 32):
            raise ValueError('Caller must provide pool32 or explicit fallback')
        pool = pool32[valid]
        with torch.no_grad():
            pool_scores = score_pairs(features.detach(), pool)
            if pool_scores.shape != pool.shape:
                raise ValueError('Scoring adapter returned incorrect shape')
            if not bool(torch.isfinite(pool_scores).all()):
                raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite pool scores')
            order = torch.argsort(pool_scores, dim=-1,
                                  descending=True, stable=True)
            ranks = torch.tensor([8, 12, 16, 20], device=order.device)
            selected_indices = order.index_select(1, ranks)
            selected = pool.gather(1, selected_indices)
        negatives = torch.cat((uniform[:, :12], selected), dim=1)
        # Caller retains only bounded records, not every training batch.
        selection_record = {
            'pool_ids': pool.detach(),
            'pool_scores': pool_scores.detach(),
            'selected_indices': selected_indices.detach(),
        }

    if bool(((negatives == 0) | (negatives == mask_id) |
             (negatives == targets[:, None])).any()):
        raise ValueError('Ineligible PAD, MASK or target negative')

    candidates = torch.cat((targets[:, None], negatives), dim=1)
    logits = score_pairs(features, candidates)
    if logits.shape != candidates.shape:
        raise ValueError('Scoring adapter returned incorrect shape')
    if not bool(torch.isfinite(logits).all()):
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite candidate logits')
    labels = torch.zeros(targets.numel(), dtype=torch.long,
                         device=logits.device)
    losses = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels, reduction='none')
    return losses, logits.detach(), candidates.detach(), selection_record


# Host integration, declared before viewing treatment validation:
# 1. Audit the corrected baseline and preserve its anchor configuration.
# 2. Declare uniform-K16 and curriculum-K16 CE comparisons, reductions,
#    replacement/overlap rules, fallbacks, RNG streams and budget.
# 3. For each configuration and all four categories, initialize one model
#    independently with seed 42; preserve preprocessing seed 0 and splits.
# 4. Use at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch.
#    Preserve windows, corruption, terminal allocation, optimizer,
#    validation schedule, stopping and checkpoint-selection policy.
# 5. Generate uniform candidates and extra pools with isolated RNG streams.
#    Apply declared small-catalog fallback outside the core helper.
# 6. Use a verified host-specific scoring adapter; do not change ModelView.
#    Apply baseline across-target/example reduction to returned losses.
# 7. Capture at most four actually consumed replay records/category,
#    including selected pool IDs/scores and same-forward reduction metadata.
# 8. Run an independent disposable one-negative diagnostic loader through
#    the preserved DiagnosisProbe and interpreter APIs; report coverage.
# 9. Save one selected checkpoint/category and emit matching predict.py.
#    Append MASK and read the greatest nonpadding index at inference.
#    Measure fresh-process reload parity if a runner is available.
# 10. Obtain pinned host validation measurements; report sampled-benchmark
#     gains, runtime, duplicates and all inspected alternatives honestly.
# 11. Bootstrap paired host user hits only if supplied; freeze selection
#     before untouched final evaluation. Never fuse models/checkpoints.

originality.positive: A precisely declared BERT4Rec sampling ablation and production-linked diagnostic protocol can provide useful task-specific evidence.
originality.negative: Model-scored negatives, rank-based selection and curricula are established techniques; the fixed warm-up and rank choices are hypotheses rather than a new hardness principle.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can guide subsequent positive-conditioned sampling and context-modeling research while preserving one network per category.
future_potential.negative: The fixed schedule lacks positive-specific adaptation, may amplify false negatives or popularity shortcuts, and has no demonstrated transfer to full-catalog user usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The learning intervention remains localized to candidate construction and loss inputs, preserving the backbone and deployed inference path.
code_difficulty.negative: Scoring-adapter compatibility, replacement semantics, isolated RNGs, bounded provenance transport, functioning diagnostics, compute controls and complete four-category comparisons require substantial integration beyond the core helper.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Provides the retained backbone and rationale for hiding supervised targets.
limitations: Does not establish benefits of the proposed negative curriculum on the pinned benchmark.
Its architecture does not remove the need to audit the supplied host sampler, reductions and predictor.

related_work.title: Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling
contributions: Selects negatives from a sampled pool using a positive-dependent target score and adjustable hardness.
Reports harder negatives earlier and easier negatives later as positive confidence increases, motivating scrutiny of epoch-only curricula.
Provides comparisons with uniform, hardest-candidate, controllable-rank and curriculum sampling.
limitations: Evidence concerns matrix factorization with BPR rather than masked BERT4Rec candidate cross-entropy.
Does not validate the proposed twenty-epoch uniform warm-up or fixed moderate ranks.
False-negative mitigation is inferred rather than established using verified negative labels.

related_work.title: Parameter-Efficiently Leveraging Session Information
contributions: The supplied search summary describes session tokens, segment embeddings and temporal attention as contextual modeling mechanisms.
limitations: Provides architectural motivation rather than evidence for stronger recency weighting under this task.
The supplied history-sensitivity outcomes are omitted, so they cannot justify a temporal direction.

related_work.title: Q-BERT4Rec
contributions: The supplied search summary connects semantic representations, quantization and masking strategies to BERT4Rec extensions.
limitations: Does not establish gains for a lightweight text encoder jointly trained from random initialization under this protocol.
A content extension must mask complete target input representations and update checkpoint and predictor implementations.

related_work.title: Rawat et al. (2021): sampled-softmax bias and sampling tradeoffs
contributions: Provides theoretical context for how negative sampling affects softmax approximation and learning.
Motivates distinguishing a sampler-dependent ranking objective from a faithful full-catalog likelihood estimator.
limitations: Does not supply the selection probabilities of the proposed rank-based mixture automatically.
Does not establish that this curriculum improves the pinned HR@10 benchmark.

related_work.title: Shi et al. (2023): hard-negative sampling and partial AUC
contributions: Provides a theoretical connection between hard-negative sampling and partial-AUC optimization for BPR.
limitations: The BPR result does not establish an equivalent interpretation for multi-negative candidate cross-entropy.
Does not verify the proposed hardness schedule or identify true negatives.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes the deterministically included positive from sampled negatives.
Develops a revised sampling correction involving model uncertainty.
limitations: Does not justify using uniform logQ values for model-ranked selected candidates.
Sampling correction does not identify genuine dislikes or eliminate false-negative uncertainty.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking evaluation can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog evaluation, including in expectation.
Explains why small candidate samples can blur distinctions between ranking metrics.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator.
Fixed users and negatives support controlled sampled-benchmark comparisons without establishing full-catalog superiority.

related_work.title: Bootstrap resampling methodology
contributions: Provides methodological grounding for paired resampling when comparing systems on shared evaluation observations.
Supports preserving paired outcomes while recomputing a comparison statistic.
limitations: The within-category paired macro-HR bootstrap is an application to this task, not a result demonstrated for this benchmark.
Conditional intervals exclude training-seed variation, candidate variation and adaptive model-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of finite-sample model-selection criteria and resulting performance-estimation bias.
Motivates recording adaptive search and reserving an untouched final evaluation.
limitations: Ordinary bootstrap intervals after adaptive search do not correct this bias.
Does not quantify selection bias for the supplied trials without their full search record.

related_work.title: Chen et al. (2022): false-negative issues in recommendation sampling
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies false-negative harm when unobserved items are repeatedly penalized during recommendation training.
limitations: Does not establish that moderate-ranked pool entries are genuine negatives.
Does not directly validate the proposed BERT4Rec curriculum or its false-negative mitigation.
